tensions: The real disagreement is cash discipline versus conviction. We are effectively fully invested with $1.87 of dry powder, which means the strongest signals on the board — DOT breaking out, ZEC in a 126% monthly move — are unactionable. The no-trim rule protects the long thesis, but it is also why we can neither add to strength nor average down on NEAR. Second tension: alt breadth is expanding hard (DOT +43%, ZEC +41%, NEAR +21% on the week) while BTC dominance holds 58.4% and total market cap fell 2.4% in 24 hours. That is either the healthy start of a rotation or a late-cycle blow-off in the long tail. F&G at 69 and declining is the one number arguing for the second reading.

opening.text: Book marks $1,397.05 against $1,086 of cost — up 28.6%. Seven of eight positions green. BTC $78,523, dominance 58.4%, Fear & Greed 69 and easing off 71 yesterday. Greedy tape, not a euphoric one.

DOT is the story. $0.908 to $1.247 in four days: +37.3% for us, +17.1% today alone, +43.3% on the week. ZEC is right behind at +24.5% held, with +41.2% over seven days and +126.1% over thirty. Two live bids — Polkadot ecosystem and privacy — and neither has cracked.

NEAR is the lone red at -5.9% from a $2.4534 entry two days ago. But NEAR is +20.6% on the week, which means we bought a local high inside an uptrend, not a broken thesis. Entry-timing error, not a sell signal. LINK +6.7%, SOL +11.2%, LTC +4.2%, AAVE +3.0%, ADA +3.0% grinding underneath.

Buying power came back at $1.87, not the ~$46.60 the playbook carried. Flagged. With no deployable cash and no broken theses, this is an eight-for-eight hold. No trims on DOT or ZEC regardless of the run — the mandate is to ride, not to harvest.
